title: bug: archive_epic shelves a BLOCKED task another seat holds, which archive_task refuses to the same caller, and records no actor on TASK_ARCHIVED, so #general reads "Task moved to ARCHIVED by unknown" (the archive_task fix 2e3012b9 never reached its sibling)
description:
Filed by defect hunt #7 (task-44785c82, architect-1dd28c7c). Reproduced on moe/work-2026-10-24 22348856; the tool files are unchanged at c89e4c59.

PROBLEM (packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/):
- Sibling archive_task (archiveTask.ts):
  - :71-77 refuses a held PLANNING/BLOCKED row (HOLDER_ONLY_FROM, :18) when the caller's workerId is not the holder. A caller with no workerId (a human) is allowed.
  - :79 passes params.workerId as the TASK_ARCHIVED actor (2e3012b9).
- Member archive_epic (archiveEpic.ts):
  - Its schema (:19-26) has no workerId. The proxy injects one anyway, McpAdapter does not enforce additionalProperties, and the handler ignores it.
  - Its IN_FLIGHT gate (:12) covers only PLANNING/AWAITING_APPROVAL/WORKING, so a BLOCKED task passes with no holder check.
  - :64 calls `state.updateTask(task.id, archiveUpdates(task), 'TASK_ARCHIVED')` with no 4th (actor) argument.
- Effect:
  - An architect's or governor's archive_epic shelves a task that a resourceId block keeps parked on worker-x. The same caller's archive_task on that row is refused "held by worker-x". archiveUpdates also clears blockedResourceId, so the lease grant can no longer restore the row.
  - Every TASK_ARCHIVED that archive_epic writes has no workerId, so get_activity_log { workerId } misses it.
  - #general reads "Task moved to ARCHIVED by unknown". For a held row it names the assignee instead, because the notice falls back to assignedWorkerId (mem:gotcha-task-event-actor-inventory).

EVIDENCE: repro at /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-44785c82/A/archiveEpic.holderActor.test.ts, run in a git-archive snapshot (/tmp/hunt-44785c82-A/packages/moe-daemon):
`LOG_LEVEL=silent npx vitest run src/tools/archiveTask.test.ts src/tools/archiveEpic.holderActor.test.ts`
- The archive_task baseline passes: it refuses the non-holder with "held by worker-x".
- FAIL "archive_epic applies the same holder-only refusal to the same caller": expected { outcome: 'rejected', taskStatus: 'BLOCKED' }, got { outcome: 'resolved', taskStatus: 'ARCHIVED' }.
- FAIL "archive_epic records the caller on each TASK_ARCHIVED and names it in #general": expected { archived: [ 'architect-c' ], lines: [ 'task-done: Task moved to ARCHIVED by architect-c' ] }, got archived [ null ] and "task-done: Task moved to ARCHIVED by unknown".

FIX DIRECTION:
- Add workerId to archive_epic's schema, worded like archive_task's.
- Extend the all-or-nothing gate before the first write. Refuse NOT_ALLOWED, naming the task and its holder, when any not-yet-archived BLOCKED task in the epic is assigned to a seat other than a caller that has a workerId. That is archive_task's exact condition: reuse HOLDER_ONLY_FROM by exporting it from archiveTask.ts, rather than copying it.
- Pass params.workerId as the 4th argument of each updateTask(..., 'TASK_ARCHIVED', ...). Never record a placeholder; a caller-less call records no workerId.
- Touch docs/MCP_SERVER.md's archive_epic section only if it contradicts the new rule. Check lanes first, because that file is often held.

FILES: packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/archiveEpic.ts; packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/archiveTask.ts (export only); new packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/archiveEpic.holderActor.test.ts (adopt the repro).
definitionOfDone: In a git-archive snapshot outside the shared checkout, `npx vitest run src/tools/archiveEpic.holderActor.test.ts` (the hunt repro, adopted) passes 3/3. archive_epic refuses an epic holding a BLOCKED task assigned to another seat, and no task in that epic changes status. Each TASK_ARCHIVED carries the caller's workerId, and #general reads "Task moved to ARCHIVED by <caller>".
A test pins the allowed paths. archive_epic with no workerId (a human) still archives that epic, and so does the holder itself. A caller-less call records no workerId on TASK_ARCHIVED.
In that snapshot, `npx vitest run src/tools/archiveEpic.test.ts src/tools/archiveTask.test.ts src/tools/taskMoveActor.test.ts` stays green.

implementationPlan.description:
IMPLEMENT (GREEN) in packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/archiveTask.ts and packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/archiveEpic.ts.
- archiveTask.ts: export only. Line 18 becomes `export const HOLDER_ONLY_FROM: TaskStatus[] = ['PLANNING', 'BLOCKED'];`. Nothing else in that file changes: its handler, wording and actor stay exactly as 2e3012b9 left them.
- archiveEpic.ts:
 1. Import `{ archiveUpdates, HOLDER_ONLY_FROM }` from './archiveTask.js'. Never copy the status list.
 2. inputSchema: add `workerId: { type: 'string', description: 'Caller worker ID (auto-injected by proxy); recorded as the actor of each TASK_ARCHIVED, and a BLOCKED row held by another worker may only be archived by its holder' }`, worded like archive_task's. Keep `required: ['epicId']` and `additionalProperties: false`. The params type becomes `{ epicId?: string; workerId?: string }`.
 3. Holder check, with explicit error handling. Right after the existing IN_FLIGHT refusal (:42-50), and BEFORE the assertNoFinalizingAttempt loop (:55-57) and the first write, compute `const held = tasksInEpic.filter((t) => HOLDER_ONLY_FROM.includes(t.status) && t.assignedWorkerId && params.workerId && params.workerId !== t.assignedWorkerId);`. That is archive_task's exact condition (archiveTask.ts:71-72). A BLOCKED row is never ARCHIVED, so already-archived rows never match. If held is non-empty, throw `notAllowed('archive epic', ...)` (NOT_ALLOWED, -32003). Its reason names the epic and every held row with its holder, e.g. `Epic "${params.epicId}" has ${held.length} BLOCKED task(s) held by another worker (${held.map((t) => `${t.id} held by ${t.assignedWorkerId}`).join(', ')}). Only each holder, or a caller with no workerId (a human), may archive them; or move them first via moe.set_task_status.` Nothing is written before the throw, so the epic and every task stay unchanged: all-or-nothing, like the IN_FLIGHT and finalizing gates. PLANNING stays refused by IN_FLIGHT for every caller; do not relax it. HOLDER_ONLY_FROM's PLANNING entry is unreachable here.
 4. Actor: line 64 becomes `await state.updateTask(task.id, archiveUpdates(task), 'TASK_ARCHIVED', params.workerId);`. Pass the bare params.workerId, never a placeholder ('unknown', 'human', 'agent' or the assignee). A caller-less call passes undefined and records no workerId (mem:gotcha-task-event-actor-inventory). An explicit '' passes through as it does in archive_task; normalizing it is out of scope. updateEpic stays as is.
 5. Tool description string: add the new refusal, e.g. '... Refuses if any task is in-flight (PLANNING/AWAITING_APPROVAL/WORKING), so release or move those first, or, for a caller with a workerId, if a BLOCKED task is held by another worker (archive_task's holder-only rule). Idempotent.'
Keep the existing comments accurate. Update the IN_FLIGHT doc comment only if it now misleads.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: moe.archive_epic applies moe.archive_task's holder-only rule and actor attribution. When a caller whose workerId names another worker targets an epic that holds a BLOCKED task assigned to that other worker, the call is refused NOT_ALLOWED (-32003) before any write. The message names each held task and its holder, and the epic and every task stay unchanged. Every TASK_ARCHIVED it writes carries the caller's bare workerId as the event actor, so get_activity_log { workerId } finds it and #general reads 'Task moved to ARCHIVED by <caller>'. A caller with no workerId (a human) and the holder itself still archive the epic, and a caller-less call records no workerId.
acceptanceCriteria: In a git-archive snapshot, npx vitest run src/tools/archiveEpic.holderActor.test.ts passes 3/3. archive_epic refuses an epic holding a BLOCKED task assigned to another seat, and no task in that epic, nor the epic, changes status. Each TASK_ARCHIVED carries the caller's workerId, and #general reads 'Task moved to ARCHIVED by <caller>'.

A test in archiveEpic.test.ts pins the allowed paths. A caller-less call (a human) and the holder still archive such an epic, and so does any caller when the BLOCKED row is unassigned. A caller-less call records no workerId on TASK_ARCHIVED.
In that snapshot, npx vitest run src/tools/archiveEpic.test.ts src/tools/archiveTask.test.ts src/tools/taskMoveActor.test.ts stays green, and so does src/state/attemptHandback.test.ts.
invariants: All-or-nothing: no task or epic write happens before every gate (IN_FLIGHT, holder, finalizing) has passed.
The TASK_ARCHIVED actor is the bare params.workerId; never 'unknown', 'agent', 'human' or the assignee.
archive_epic and archive_task share one holder-only status list (HOLDER_ONLY_FROM) and one archiveUpdates.
compatibility: workerId is optional and additive: required stays ['epicId'] and additionalProperties stays false. The result shape {success, epicId, epicStatus, archivedTaskCount, totalTasks} is unchanged.
A caller with no workerId (a human) keeps today's behaviour. The board has no archive_epic path; it uses ARCHIVE_DONE_TASKS.
No .moe/ state shape change. archiveUpdates and the BLOCKED clear-on-exit fields are unchanged.
PLANNING/AWAITING_APPROVAL/WORKING stay refused by the IN_FLIGHT gate for every caller. The ATTEMPT_FINALIZING gate is unchanged.
